issues.description: The predicate complects two facts about the layer node into a negated conjunction inside a larger boolean.
issues.detail: The condition `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` reads as a double negative buried in a five-clause `&&` chain. A named predicate like `isLayerStatement(node)` (layer without a block) would separate the fact from the filter, making the rule about values, not boolean gymnastics.

issues.description: Using `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` conflates 'no block' with 'property happens to be undefined'.
issues.detail: PostCSS models a block as the presence of `nodes` (an array). The intent is 'layer statement form' vs 'layer block form' — a fact about the AST. Checking `node.nodes` directly (or `Array.isArray`) names that fact; `typeof ... === 'undefined'` is an easy idiom that hides what's being asked.

issues.description: Test coverage exercises only one shape of the new fact; the dual case is left implicit.
issues.detail: The added test covers `@layer foo {}` before `@import`. The complementary case — `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import`, which must remain valid — is the other half of the distinction this patch introduces. Asserting both pins down the value semantics rather than just the bug repro.

review.summary: The fix is correct and minimal: it stops treating every `@layer` as import-compatible and only excuses the statement form. That is the right decomposition of the underlying fact — layer-with-block is a side effect that anchors position, layer-without-block is a declaration that doesn't. The implementation, though, encodes that fact as a negated conjunction with `typeof ... === 'undefined'` inside an already dense predicate, which is easy-not-simple: it works, but the meaning is complected with the filter. A named predicate and a symmetric statement-form test would make the value semantics explicit. SIMPLE in intent, mildly EASY-NOT-SIMPLE in expression.
